## Why
Agents send code and multi-line briefs into other tabs all day. Today a backslash-n in the text becomes a real newline, an unknown flag is typed into the terminal, and the words `delivered`, `queued`, and `submitted` are not in the skill. A caller cannot tell a paste the PTY accepted from one waiting on attach, or from one the agent has actually seen. Backlog item: C3.

## Evidence
- c11: `CLI/c11.swift:2947-2976` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) parses `--workspace`, `--surface`, and `--no-submit` for `send`, then joins the remainder and runs `unescapeSendText` (`:11923-11929`), which rewrites `\n`, `\r`, and `\t`. There is no stdin form. An unknown `--flag` in that remainder is part of the text.
- c11: `sendTextSummary` (`:5224-5228`) appends `queued=1` only when the payload says queued. It does not mention `delivered` or `submitted`.
- c11: `Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift:846-980`. `v2SurfaceSendText` sets `submitted`, `queued`, and `delivered` (`:977-979`). `delivered` is `!queued`. `Sources/TerminalController.swift:6643-6727` (`deliverSocketSendText`) pastes prose through `ghostty_surface_text`, strips trailing newlines, and schedules one Return after the paste-settle delay. `submitted` means that Return was dispatched, not that the agent consumed it.
- Upstream: cmux #13849, #14837, #14937. `cmux paste` reads an argument or stdin, rejects unknown flags, and returns `delivery: delivered|queued`. `--submit` sends an agent-aware key later. A failed submit returns `submitted: false` and is not an error.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1d. Fable row 4.4 and Astra row 4.4 (core). Astra's acceptance line: literal backslashes and trailing newlines obey the documented mode, and a queued paste is never reported as an agent-acknowledged message.
- Overlap: C11-140 section B already says `send` does not reject unknown flags (`c11 send --text "hi"` types `--text hi`). That audit ticket stays the June 2026 I/O list (UTF-8 framing, short writes, the focus-allowance stack). This ticket owns the 1.0 delivery contract, including that one bullet, so it is not done twice.

## Scope
In: `c11 send --raw` (no escape rewriting), `c11 send -` to read stdin, and `c11 paste` as a documented alias of `send --raw`. Reject unknown `--flags` before the text is assembled. Document `delivered`, `queued`, and `submitted` in `skills/c11/references/api.md`, with the meanings in Evidence. Default `send` keeps today's escape rewriting.
Out: the draft guard (backlog A5). Long `launch-agent` prompts (C11-258, backlog C8). The bracketed-paste split across terminal replies (bug harvest #4, Ghostty). Byte-exact delivery of C0 controls. `socketTextIsPasteDeliverable` (`TerminalController.swift:6662-6673`) still sends those as key events, because Ghostty's paste encoder replaces them with spaces. Do not promise byte-exact for those. cmux's ctrl+enter upgrade for multi-line Claude Code. The skill already says a multi-line send arrives as one turn. Verify that on a tagged build before porting anything. If it holds, do not port the upgrade. `new-workspace --command`'s discarded send result moves to C2 with `initial_input`. Do not re-add a follow-up send here.

## Approach
Parse flags up to `--`. Unknown `--name` is a CLI error. `--raw` skips `unescapeSendText`. `-` with no other text reads stdin. `paste` calls the same path as `send --raw` and accepts the same targeting flags. Keep `--no-submit`. Human output names the three states in words, not only `queued=1`. JSON already returns the booleans. Leave them. Update the c11 skill and sync the installed copy on the landing machine. Register feature flag `send.raw` if C6's list exists. Comment on C11-140 when the PR opens, pointing the unknown-flag bullet here.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `c11 send --tab <t> --raw 'printf %s \n'` delivers the four characters backslash, n, to the terminal. The same call without `--raw` delivers a newline, as today.
2. `c11 send --tab <t> --bogus hello` exits non-zero, prints an error that names `--bogus`, and the tab's screen does not contain `--bogus`. This is the C11-140 bullet.
3. `printf 'line1\nline2\n' | c11 paste --tab <t> --no-submit` inserts both lines and does not submit. `c11 paste --help` describes it as `send --raw`.
4. Against a tab whose PTY is not attached yet, the JSON has `queued: true`, `delivered: false`. The human line does not say the agent saw it. After attach, the text is in the scrollback. Against an attached shell, `delivered: true`. With submit, `submitted: true` means the Return was scheduled, and the skill says so.
5. A multi-line `c11 send` into a Claude Code tab on a tagged build becomes one turn. Record the result. Port a ctrl+enter submit only if that run shows the submit was swallowed.

## Validation
`c11LogicTests` or a CLI-level test for flag parsing and `--raw`, if a seam exists that does not boot the app. A `tests_v2` script against a tagged build for criteria 1 through 4. Criterion 5 is one computer-use or `read-screen` check on a real Claude Code tab. No soak. Do not claim the agent processed the text.

## Dependencies
Related to C2. C11-140 section B holds the unknown-flag note. C11-173 (done) is the paste-submit path this builds on. Do not reopen it. Feature flag name lives with C6.

## Risks
Typing latency: CLI-side parsing only. Do not add work to `deliverSocketSendText` beyond the raw/unescape choice, which happens before the socket call. Main thread: `tab.send_text` is already a socket-worker method (`SocketDispatch.swift:64-65`). Leave it there. Doctrine: no tenant config writes. Localization: new CLI errors use `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: document the three states. Do not describe Ghostty's control-byte stripping as an attack note. One sentence in the skill is enough.

Size: S–M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: `send` reports what c11 did with the bytes. It does not report what the agent thought.

# C11-281 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL** at `c8c04ea982293d0e723d8975b9d021b38df554ee`.

PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/519

Base: `2d2440ac65425b0041aad2b3117f6c1c5e612768`, the merge-base with freshly fetched origin/main. PR head and detached checkout still match the commissioned head. Review checkout is clean. Reviewed all 15 changed files and the CLI transport, socket dispatch, attached/queued input, and event-emission seams. No builds, tests, product changes, or live input probes were performed by this reviewer.

## Blocking

1. **Raw mode still implicitly submits.** `Sources/SendTextParse.swift:17,45-48`; `CLI/c11.swift:3042`; `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:207`. `c11 send --tab <target> --raw 'echo example'` leaves `submit = true`, so it schedules a separate Return and executes the line. The same is true of `paste`. The live test expressly expects an extra Return for `send --raw -`, without any explicit submit option. This contradicts this cycle's review brief: raw sends the given bytes with no implicit Return. The stored implementation plan and current documentation instead preserve default submission and require `--no-submit`; this is a concrete contract disagreement, not an undiscovered runtime edge. Smallest fix under the review brief: make raw/paste suppress the extra Return by default, preserve ordinary send's existing default, and update behavioral tests/help/skill accordingly. Explicit `send-key enter` already supplies submission. If the release owner intends the plan's different contract, the review brief needs an explicit correction before this can pass. The ticket's stated C0-control exclusion remains valid; this finding concerns the additional Return.

2. **The new large UTF-8 stdin path crosses a lossy framing seam, with no large-input proof.** `CLI/c11.swift:3040-3051` sends the whole stdin string through JSON to the unchanged `Sources/TerminalController.swift:2030-2039`. That reader decodes each at-most-4095-byte socket read independently, replacing the entire chunk with an empty string if UTF-8 decoding fails. A long stdin document containing multibyte characters can split one character across reads; both fragments fail decoding, discarding whole chunks. The outcome can be invalid JSON or missing document text. `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:204-208` exercises only tiny ASCII inputs; the retained runtime driver invokes those same cases. Thus the brief's large-text/no-truncation requirement is neither established nor supported by the full path. This is a statically identified inherited seam, not a claimed new regression or an executed reproduction. Smallest fix: coordinate with C11-140's existing framing ownership, preserve bytes until a complete newline-delimited request is assembled, then decode; add an Atlas behavioral case that forces UTF-8 splits and compares the complete large stdin payload at the PTY. No new ticket or wider I/O rewrite is needed.

3. **Queued newline/no-submit acceptance remains unproved.** `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:239-256`. The actual queue scenario sends a literal backslash+n string and a suffix, then checks screen text and absence of `command not found`. It never queues real leading/trailing/newline-only content or stdin, and does not inspect bytes or Return outside the paste envelope after flush. The two host tests inspect the pending queue before attach; they do not exercise the eventual Ghostty/PTY flush. Plan acceptance 3 explicitly requires repeating the newline cases on the queued-before-attach path. The existing proof would miss newline conversion or an extra Return during attach. Smallest fix: extend the bounded queue fixture's Atlas runtime proof to those inputs with an exact byte/Return oracle across flush, retaining full-text events and queued/delivered booleans. This is a missing required proof, not a claim that the new queue helper is demonstrably broken.

## Non-blocking

1. Correct the owner evidence's Claude version attribution: retained composer screens identify **2.1.287**, while the report and proof driver hard-code **2.1.284**. Record the observed version rather than a constant. This does not invalidate the visible draft and one-turn observations.

## Evidence reviewed

Owner validation comment: `ev_01M3XSHTG7F1X2J6QRJQATG5F7`.

The retained Atlas test manifest `build-remote/ba64d4aff9254ef691c64108746396ec/result.json` identifies the exact clean head; its build log records 17 passing tests, including the built CLI fixtures and two pending-queue tests. These are behavioral tests, not source-grep substitutes. The guide-test modification reads the built bundle's plist, consistent with the repository policy.

The tagged artifact manifest `build-remote/b5b0375e79fb4806b84e71f3caf1b796/result.json`, retained runtime driver and final smoke log establish the owner's clean-source artifact attribution, matching running/retained executable, dylib and CLI hashes, and the attached PTY plus actual queue runs. CLI/server commit identities are null in this artifact; they are not represented as matching stamped SHAs. The typed registry enables send.raw version 1 and both admission paths consult it.

The C11-257 event emitter call and full text/caller fields remain intact. The retained attached and queued tests assert one attributed tab.input_sent per request. No mailbox transaction implementation or tenant configuration is changed. The DEBUG queue fixture is bounded, per-tab, and compiled out of Release. No human keystroke-path work was added. Default send's decoding/trailing-newline policy is preserved by the shared delivery policy; unknown long flags are rejected before connection/delivery.

The retained composer screens and synthetic turn records support an unsubmitted raw draft until explicit Return, followed by one user turn, and one complete default multi-line user turn. **The expired login does not matter for that acceptance:** it asks whether input became one turn, not whether the model responded. No model response or acknowledgment is proved or required. These are owner-produced artifacts inspected by this reviewer, not an independent runtime rerun.

## Runtime proof still required

Before landing, Atlas must demonstrate the corrected raw default without an extra Return; complete large ASCII and multibyte UTF-8 stdin delivery across transport read boundaries; and queued leading/interior/trailing/newline-only content across attach with an exact Return boundary oracle. Repeat the changed cases on the resulting head, preserving raw capability parity and one full attributed event per send. Keep default send compatibility and unknown-flag non-delivery checks.

The current exact-head GitHub build and compatibility checks remain in progress, and mailbox-unit is queued. They are not green evidence; the Merge Captain still needs the required exact-head checks before landing. The paired latency samples were collected under differing host load and are not a performance-pass claim. No additional model-response run is required to resolve the expired login.

Orchestrator on review ev_01M3XT05X0BD50W1B5M3B33RYW: finding 1 waived; the Orchestrator's review brief was wrong. The ticket contract is --raw = no escape rewriting, default submit preserved, --no-submit to suppress (Scope line 21/25, AC3). Findings 2 (UTF-8 chunk split in the socket reader for large stdin) and 3 (queued-before-attach newline/no-submit proof) stand.

C11-281 repair round 1 at aabd639e92e3a4776f288ef86415f76c8fee4e57 (clean source; one repair commit). Review ev_01M3XT05X0BD50W1B5M3B33RYW. Finding 1 waived by the Orchestrator: default submit remains; --no-submit suppresses Return.

Finding 2: TerminalController.serveCommandLines retains raw Data until newline and decodes each complete request once. Per-read autoreleasepool, auth/response dispatch and partial-frame EOF behavior remain. No new protocol, size policy, thread or main hop. This repairs the inherited framing seam also identified by C11-140.

Atlas final-head actual test action: invocation 015b2e2da83341db843bf836b953b1b8, clean matching head, compile/tests ok. All 14 executed tests passed: seven send parser/protocol tests (including built-CLI fixtures), two registry tests, three SocketClientCommandLoopTests, and two host pending-queue tests. The command loop exercised a 40958-byte multibyte request with read-limit boundaries inside UTF-8, a following request on the same connection, framing/blank-line handling and autorelease release while the connection stays open.

Tagged final-head Debug artifact: 2215165ebf0f45419f8ad4357f216122, compile ok, clean matching manifest head. Fresh Atlas PID 24653. Running executable, debug dylib and bundled CLI all matched the retained remote artifact. CLI/server commit stamps are null; source attribution is through the clean remote manifest and matching three file hashes, not a fabricated capabilities SHA.
- Executable d9d14d3d5085b3eac2cf1b15b34c965de20cd4e2dc00b1d6cc0dcdc85108a5be.
- Debug dylib 873f5b7dd22ea189ff79afb493b3747b1c5a470787a4a425cdbc5c11d5fa4d54.
- Bundled CLI ab382e2ae22a443b903894f1808dbd15f53db4b48be83bbe0297dede24ca57dc.

Live built-CLI/PTy proof passed: 65555-byte ASCII stdin; 73738-byte Unicode stdin (界🙂é repeated, with a newline footer). The Unicode CLI request was 74029 wire bytes; the transparent proxy sent an incomplete UTF-8 fragment ending at byte 4001, paused 150 ms, then forwarded the remainder in <=4095-byte chunks. Exact complete paste bytes matched at the raw PTY collector, with no external Return for --no-submit. Each request had one complete attributed event with the original body. Default escaping/trailing-newline compatibility, unknown-flag non-delivery, send.raw version 1, and the original automatic queue timeout/attach case also passed.

All five actual queued-before-attach byte/Return cases passed on this artifact: leading/interior/trailing newline content (27 bytes, no Return); newline-only positional raw (1 byte, no Return); raw stdin with newlines and Unicode (14 bytes, no Return); newline-only paste stdin (1 byte, no Return); default-submit raw stdin (11 bytes, exactly one Return outside paste). Responses asserted queued:true, delivered:false and effective submitted state; one full caller-attributed queued event per input. Each case used a fresh inactive workspace, cleaned up after proof.

Historical attempts: 3e8932acd20d4ce0bef331637cb6329c failed before compile on Atlas disk-full slot admission; Orchestrator fixed disk, no shared artifacts were deleted by this owner. Initial 0d2de4f397 tests (12) and large-input/automatic-attach/first queued-byte cases passed, but later queued cases reused a visible workspace, triggering immediate eager attachment. Corrected the harness and its cleanup, amended the unpublished repair to one final commit, and repeated every required case at aabd639e92. Superseded pre-admission test 38556f491b3c4f48baa2c760e223cd93 was cancelled; no tests from it are claimed.

Finding 3: preserve the original automatic-attach scenario, and extend the bounded per-tab DEBUG fixture with a ten-second pending-flush hold. Input queues through the real pre-attach handler timeout, then the PTY collector starts after runtime attach before explicit release invokes the production queue flush. This staged byte proof distinguishes queue admission from terminal attach/flush; it does not claim the collector existed before the PTY. The original scenario separately checks automatic attach without the additional hold. The fixture is compiled out of Release, does no keystroke/hitTest/forceRefresh work, and automatically releases both holds.

Correction to ev_01M3XSHTG7F1X2J6QRJQATG5F7: retained real Claude composer screens identify 2.1.287, not the driver's hard-coded 2.1.284. Earlier exact c8c04e evidence for draft until explicit Return and one full user turn remains historical; it was not rerun as part of this transport repair and no model response is claimed. This repair needs no new model-response proof.

Runtime retains smoke transcript, clean artifact-identity driver, capabilities and this exact tagged PID event log. 2. Run tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py. Expect large ASCII/fragmented UTF-8 stdin byte equality, default/unknown-flag/event compatibility, the original automatic queue attach, and five queued byte/Return PASS cases. The proxy forwards the built CLI's wire bytes unchanged and pauses inside a multibyte codepoint near the read ceiling.

# C11-281 delta review, round 2

Verdict: **PASS** at `aabd639e92e3a4776f288ef86415f76c8fee4e57`.

Reviewed only `c8c04ea982293d0e723d8975b9d021b38df554ee..aabd639e92e3a4776f288ef86415f76c8fee4e57` and the directly affected framing/queue seams. All five changed files were inspected. Detached checkout, origin branch and PR #519 match the requested head; checkout is clean. Finding 1 remains waived by the Orchestrator: raw mode retains default submit, and --no-submit suppresses the additional Return. No earlier scope was reopened.

## Blocking

None. Findings 2 and 3 are resolved; no new blocking defect found in this delta.

## Findings verified

1. **Finding 2 resolved.** `Sources/TerminalController.swift:2031-2043` accumulates Data, locates the newline delimiter as a byte, and decodes each complete request once. Incomplete multibyte characters now survive socket-read boundaries. The read/process iteration remains inside the existing autoreleasepool; authentication, response dispatch, worker placement and partial-frame EOF handling are unchanged. The added socketpair test executes the production loop with a 40,958-byte multibyte request and a second request on the same connection. Existing framing and held-connection autorelease tests also passed.

   The retained tagged runtime proof executes the built CLI with 65,555-byte ASCII stdin and 73,738-byte Unicode stdin. Its relay preserves the CLI wire bytes, deliberately pauses inside a UTF-8 sequence at byte 4,001 of a 74,029-byte request, then forwards the remaining chunks. The PTY collector compares the full paste envelope and contents byte-for-byte, including absence of an extra Return. The retained event log contains the complete two large bodies with caller attribution and submitted:false. This addresses the specific framing loss and missing large-input evidence raised in round 1.

2. **Finding 3 resolved.** `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py::queued_bytes` now proves all five commissioned cases: leading/interior/trailing newline content; newline-only positional raw; raw stdin with Unicode and newlines; newline-only paste stdin; and default-submit raw stdin. Each request is admitted through the real pre-attach handler with queued:true and delivered:false. The collector receives the exact queued bytes through the production flush, with zero extra Returns in the four no-submit cases and exactly one Return outside the paste envelope in the submit case. Each case verifies one complete caller-attributed queued event. All five PASS lines and corresponding event records are retained.

   The added flush hold is explicitly a DEBUG fixture: per-tab, bounded to ten seconds, automatically released, and absent from Release. It permits the collector to start after runtime attach before releasing the actual pending queue. It does not substitute synthetic bytes for the production flush. The original automatic-attach queue scenario remains and passed independently, so the staged byte oracle is not being presented as proof that the collector existed before PTY creation.

## Non-blocking
